target: Yol kenarında mısır satan amca her yaz orada.
english: The uncle selling corn by the road is there every summer.
tip: The ‘-an’ ending builds a describing clause: ‘mısır satan amca’ = the uncle who sells corn. ‘satan’ describes ‘amca’.

target: Babamın arabası tamirde.
english: My father's car is being repaired.
tip: Possession pairs two endings: the owner gets ‘-ın’, the thing gets ‘-sı’, giving ‘babamın arabası’ = my father's car.

target: Arkadaşım Ankara'da bir hastanede çalışıyor.
english: My friend works at a hospital in Ankara.
tip: Proper names take an apostrophe before a case ending: ‘Ankara'da’ = in Ankara. Common nouns skip it, like ‘hastanede’.

target: Garson plajda kaybettiği anahtarı sabırla buldu.
english: The waiter patiently found the key he had lost at the beach.
tip: The ‘-diği’ ending builds a past describing clause on an object: ‘kaybettiği anahtar’ = the key that he lost.

target: Çiftçi tiyatroda sessizce oturdu.
english: The farmer sat quietly at the theater.
tip: The ‘-ce’ ending turns an adjective into a manner adverb: ‘sessizce’ = quietly, from ‘sessiz’ = quiet.

target: Onlar henüz gelmedi.
english: They haven't come yet.
tip: ‘henüz’ means 'yet'. With a negative verb like ‘gelmedi’ it means 'not yet': ‘onlar henüz gelmedi’ = they haven't come yet.

target: Arkadaşımdan mektup geldi.
english: A letter came from my friend.
tip: The suffix ‘-dan/-den’ marks the source, 'from': ‘arkadaşımdan’ = from my friend.

target: Ali okuldan eve mutlulukla döndü.
english: Ali happily returned home from school.
tip: Add ‘-la/-le’ to a noun to make a manner adverb: ‘mutluluk’ (happiness) plus ‘-la’ gives ‘mutlulukla’ = happily.

target: Markete ekmek almaya gittim.
english: I went to the market to buy bread.
tip: Verb stem plus ‘-maya/-meye’ shows purpose, 'in order to': ‘almaya’ = to buy, telling why you ‘gittim’ (went).

target: Sıradan bir müdür fırının yanında duruyor.
english: An ordinary manager is standing next to the bakery.
tip: ‘yanında’ means 'next to'; the noun before it takes the owner ending ‘-ın’: ‘fırının yanında’ = next to the bakery.

target: Bugün çok yorgunum, erken yatacağım.
english: I'm very tired today, I'll go to bed early.
tip: The suffix ‘-acak/-ecek’ makes the future tense: ‘yat-’ (go to bed) plus ‘-acağım’ gives ‘yatacağım’ = I will go to bed.

target: Denize yakın bir otel arıyoruz.
english: We're looking for a hotel close to the sea.
tip: ‘yakın’ (near) needs the 'to' ending ‘-a/-e’ on what you are near: ‘denize yakın’ = close to the sea.

target: Geçen yaz Sultanahmet Camii'ni ziyaret ettik.
english: We visited the Blue Mosque last summer.
tip: ‘etmek’ turns a noun into a verb: ‘ziyaret’ (a visit) plus ‘ettik’ gives ‘ziyaret ettik’ = we visited.

target: Senin araban mı bu, çok güzel.
english: Is this your car? It's very nice.
tip: ‘mı’ is the yes/no question word; it stays separate and sits after the thing asked about: ‘araban mı’ = is it your car.

target: Her zaman dürüst olmalıyız, yalan söylememeliyiz.
english: We should always be honest, we shouldn't lie.
tip: The suffix ‘-malı/-meli’ means 'must/should': ‘olmalıyız’ = we should be, ‘söylememeliyiz’ = we shouldn't say.

target: Deniz kenarında bir tatil evi kiraladık.
english: We rented a holiday house near the sea.
tip: In a noun-plus-noun compound the second noun takes ‘-i’: ‘tatil’ (holiday) plus ‘ev’ gives ‘tatil evi’ = holiday house.

target: Hayatımın en güzel günlerini burada geçirdim.
english: I spent the best days of my life here.
tip: Put ‘en’ before an adjective to mean 'most': ‘en güzel’ = the most beautiful.

target: Bu dükkanın vitrinindeki elbise çok güzel.
english: The dress in this shop's window is very beautiful.
tip: Add ‘-ki’ after a place ending to mean 'the one at/in': ‘vitrinindeki’ = the one in the shop window.

target: Güzel bir gün, hava sıcak ve güneşli.
english: A beautiful day, the weather is warm and sunny.
tip: The suffix ‘-li/-lı’ means 'having': ‘güneş’ (sun) plus ‘-li’ gives ‘güneşli’ = sunny.

target: Bırak çocuk oynasın, zaten bütün gün ders çalıştı.
english: Let the child play; he's studied all day anyway.
tip: The ‘-sın’ ending gives a let-him/her command: ‘oynasın’ = let him play.

target: Ailemiz beş kişilik, anne baba ve üç çocuk.
english: Our family is five people, mother father and three children.
tip: After a number, ‘-lik’ means 'consisting of / sized for': ‘beş kişilik’ = of five people (five-person).

target: Halasının evi deniz kenarında.
english: His/Her aunt's house is by the sea.
tip: Possession links two suffixes: the owner takes ‘-ın’, the thing takes ‘-ı’: ‘halasının evi’ = his aunt's house.

target: Müdür hastaneden aceleyle ayrıldı.
english: The director hurriedly left the hospital.
tip: ‘ayrılmak’ (to leave) takes the 'from' ending ‘-den’ on the place: ‘hastaneden ayrıldı’ = left the hospital.

target: Sokaklar yağmurdan sonra ıslanmış.
english: The streets are wet after the rain.
tip: The suffix ‘-mış’ reports something inferred from evidence, not witnessed: ‘ıslanmış’ = they have gotten wet (I see the result).

target: Balkondan bakınca deniz görünüyor.
english: The sea is visible when you look from the balcony.
tip: Verb stem plus ‘-ınca/-ince’ means 'when/upon doing': ‘bakınca’ = when you look.

target: Hay Allah, çantamı evde unutmuşum.
english: Oh no, I forgot my bag at home.
tip: ‘-mış’ on your own action marks a sudden realization: ‘unutmuşum’ = oh, I've forgotten (I just noticed).

target: Babam sabahları erken kalkar ve bahçeye bakar.
english: My father gets up early in the mornings and tends the garden.
tip: The habit ending ‘-ar/-er’ states habits and general truths: ‘kalkar’ = gets up, ‘bakar’ = tends, done regularly.

target: Burada sigara içemezsiniz, yasak.
english: You can't smoke here, it's prohibited.
tip: The negative ending ‘-emez/-amaz’ means 'cannot' and often 'not allowed': ‘içemezsiniz’ = you can't smoke.

target: İstanbul, Ankara'dan daha kalabalık bir şehir.
english: Istanbul is a more crowded city than Ankara.
tip: For comparisons use ‘daha’ (more) and mark the thing compared with ‘-dan’: ‘Ankara'dan daha kalabalık’ = more crowded than Ankara.

target: Çevre kirliliğini önlemek için geri dönüşüm yapmalıyız.
english: We must recycle to prevent environmental pollution.
tip: Infinitive plus ‘için’ means 'in order to': ‘önlemek için’ = in order to prevent.
